newsitem.title: USA: Kentucky sees May boost in revenue, is on target.
newsitem.headline: Kentucky sees May boost in revenue, is on target.

text.p: Kentucky revenue collections rose by 14.1 percent in May to $408.4 million, putting the state on track to meet revenue projections for the year that ends June 30, state officials said.

For the 11 months to date, revenue collections have increased by 5.6 percent over the same period last year. Collections must increase by four percent for the year to meet projections of $5.552 billion for the year.
Sales tax collections rose by 8.2 percent in May, while individual income tax receipts rose by 28 percent and property tax receipts increased by 32.4 percent.
The state Finance Cabinet said the large increases in property and income tax receipts were partly due to early filing and processing.
